y-m-28-11.title: Two people solve x²−4x−3=0 in different ways
y-m-28-11.topic: Compare methods for solving quadratic equations
y-m-28-11.goal: Separate integer-factor method failing from no solution, and compare exact checks for radical answer.
y-m-28-11.material:
Find real solutions of x²−4x−3=0. (x² read "x squared".)
Sua: Integer pairs product −3 are (1,−3),(−1,3); sums −2,2, not −4. So no solution.
Doyun: Quadratic formula gives x=2±√7. (± means plus or minus; √7 read root seven.) 1 2 2 3
y-m-28-11.thinking.1: Separate what failed method actually tell
y-m-28-11.prereq.1: Find two integer sum given fixed product (factoring)
y-m-28-11.s.s1.hint.0: Say what type of numbers Sua method handles.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.hint.1: Write "method failed" and "no solution" separately, compare.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.o.a: This quadratic equation get no solution.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.r.a: Only factoring and matching integer sum failed; it no directly test whether solution exists.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.o.b: No integer pair match product and sum.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.r.b: This says only what attempted method shows; it no jump to no solution.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.o.c: Confirmed the 2 values Doyun found are wrong.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.r.c: Sua method only uses integer pairs. To say Doyun wrong, check his answer directly.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.r.d: No reason to think problem wrong; solving method fit have limits.
y-m-28-11.s.s1.explain: Sua only try integer factor pairs. Failure only show it cannot factor into linear terms with integer coefficients.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.prompt: What surest check whether Doyun x=2+√7 correct?
y-m-28-11.s.s2.hint.1: After adding −4x and −3, check whether √7 remain.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.o.a: Approximate √7≈2.65, put x≈4.65 and see if result near 0.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.r.a: This quick check catch big mistakes, but no prove exactly 0.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.o.b: Doyun use quadratic formula, so no need check.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.r.b: Formula solution can still have arithmetic error. Check result even if method right.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.o.c: Repeat quadratic formula same steps and see if same answer.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.r.c: Repeating same method may repeat same mistake.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.o.d: Put x=2+√7 in equation and expand to see if exactly 0.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.r.d: This uses solution meaning directly: equation true when value substituted. Radical number can be checked exactly by expanding.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.explain: (2+√7)²=11+4√7; −4(2+√7)=−8−4√7. Add: 11+4√7−8−4√7−3=0. Approximation can be quick first check.
y-m-28-11.s.s2.acc.0: Approximation is good quick filter for big errors. To prove exact solution, expand and check exact 0.
